issues.display_title: Issue #1869: feat(auth): Revoke Keycloak User Sessions on API Logout
issues.main_description_html:
Summary

Enhance POST /v1/auth/logout to clear the user's active Keycloak SSO session when logging out of GoThru.

Workflow

  1. Identify User: Before deleting the session, check if the logging-out user is linked to Keycloak (keycloak_sub).
  2. Clear Keycloak Session: If linked, call Keycloak's server-to-server admin logout endpoint to invalidate their SSO browser session.
  3. Delete GoThru Session: Remove the session from the GoThru database as usual.
  4. Resilience: Ensure GoThru logout always succeeds even if Keycloak is temporarily unavailable.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Logging out removes the session from the GoThru database.
  • Linked Keycloak accounts have their Keycloak SSO sessions revoked.
  • Accounts not linked to Keycloak log out normally without errors.
  • Handles session ID from both cookie and request body.
  • All unit tests pass.

Result

  • PR: Opened via #1868.
  • Verification: Tested with user muhamad210501@gmail.com — active Keycloak session was successfully terminated (HTTP 204), and subsequent session checks returned empty.
  • Tests: Unit test suite (LogoutActionTest) passed with 4/4 tests covering session deletion, Keycloak revocation, and graceful error handling.

issues.display_title: Issue #1870: feat(user): Provide granular CRUD endpoints for Maps JavaScript API keys
issues.main_description_html:
Summary

Provide individual RESTful CRUD endpoints for Maps JavaScript API keys (POST, PUT, DELETE on /users/map-javascript) to replace or complement the legacy bulk-synchronization endpoint (POST /users/map-javascript).

Background

The dashboard UI for Maps JavaScript API key management has been redesigned from a bulk form-save into a modern modal-driven table interface with individual Add, Edit, and Delete actions.

Currently, POST /users/map-javascript acts as a full-reconciliation sync endpoint (syncDeletedKeys + bulk upsert). Granular CRUD operations from modal dialogs currently have to submit the entire list of keys every time, risking race conditions and unnecessary payload size when users make quick edits or deletions.

Proposed Endpoints

1. POST /users/map-javascript (Create Single Key)

Create a new Maps JavaScript API key for the authenticated user.

  • Request Body: 
    {
  "name": "Production Key",
  "key": "AIzaSy...",
  "type": "global"
}
  • Validation:
    • name: required string
    • key: required string, starts with AIzaSy, min 30 chars, globally unique across users
    • type: required enum (global | tour)
  • Response (201/200): 
    {
  "status": 200,
  "message": "API key created successfully",
  "data": {
    "id": 12345,
    "name": "Production Key",
    "key": "AIzaSy...",
    "usage_location": "global"
  }
}

2. PUT /users/map-javascript/{id} (Update Single Key)

Update an existing Maps JavaScript API key.

  • Path Param: id (integer)
  • Request Body: 
    {
  "name": "Updated Key Name",
  "key": "AIzaSy...",
  "type": "tour"
}
  • Response (200): 
    {
  "status": 200,
  "message": "API key updated successfully",
  "data": {
    "id": 12345,
    "name": "Updated Key Name",
    "key": "AIzaSy...",
    "usage_location": "tour"
  }
}

3. DELETE /users/map-javascript/{id} (Delete Single Key)

Delete a specific Maps JavaScript API key belonging to the user.

  • Path Param: id (integer)
  • Response (200): 
    {
  "status": 200,
  "message": "API key deleted successfully"
}

Note: Legacy bulk endpoint (POST /users/map-javascript with maps: [...] payload) should be preserved or aliased for backwards compatibility until all clients transition.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Endpoint POST /users/map-javascript accepts single-key payload and returns created key with ID.
  • Endpoint PUT /users/map-javascript/{id} updates only the specified key belonging to the authenticated user.
  • Endpoint DELETE /users/map-javascript/{id} deletes only the specified key belonging to the authenticated user.
  • Key validation (AIzaSy prefix, length >= 30, unique check, valid type) is applied consistently.
  • Unit tests covering create, update, delete, and validation error scenarios.

Result

  • PR: Merged via #1871.
  • Frontend PR: #4280.
  • Verification:
    • Live E2E curl testing against local backend (http://localhost:8080) with real user JWT authentication (muhamad210501@gmail.com) covering single key creation (POST), update (PUT), deletion (DELETE), duplicate key rejection (HTTP 400), invalid key format rejection (HTTP 400), and non-existent key handling (HTTP 404).
    • Automated Playwright E2E recording script in frontend (qa_testing/e2e_maps_api_demo_record.js) with explicit network request synchronization (page.waitForResponse(...)).
    • 720p HD 16:9 demo video recorded at qa_testing/artifacts/maps-api-key-demo-720p.mp4 (1.4 MB).
  • Unit Tests: 19/19 tests passed across MapsJavascriptCrudActionTest, MapsJavascriptRoutesTest, and GetMapJavascriptActionTest.

issues.display_title: Issue #1874: feat(tours): Create related-by-cid API to list tours sharing the same CID that will also be archived
issues.main_description_html:
Summary

Create a new endpoint POST /v1/tours/related-by-cid that returns tours sharing the same CID as the tours being archived — i.e. the tours that will also be archived by the archive cascade worker (which runs outside gothru-new-api). The endpoint is purely informational: it must not perform any archiving itself.

Background

The Archive Tour modal (ArchiveTour.jsx) warns users: "there are other tours with the same CID — they will automatically be archived as well" and shows a related-tours table (Tour Name / CID / Total Panorama).

The archive payload only carries moderationIds (no CID), so the BE must resolve CIDs itself. The archive cascade to same-CID tours is handled by an external worker outside this project — this endpoint only feeds the warning UI.

Request

Uses the same filter payload as batch archive (POST /v1/tours/batch/archive):

{
  "type_select": "selected",
  "moderationIds": ["mid-1", "mid-2"],
  "exceptionIds": []
}
  • type_select: "all" → all tours matching the current filter minus exceptionIds are the archive targets. Note: resolving "all" requires the same query params as batch archive (tags, types, search) — the FE must forward them alongside the body.

Response

{
  "data": {
    "related_tours": [
      {
        "moderation_id": "string",
        "business_name": "string",
        "cid": "string",
        "total_panorama": 0
      }
    ]
  }
}

Requirements

  • Return only tours whose CID matches any target CID, excluding tours in moderationIds and exceptionIds (those are already the direct archive targets — the user sees them in the modal; this endpoint surfaces the additional same-CID tours the worker will also archive).
  • Empty array when no related tours exist (FE hides the warning).
  • Enforce per-user visibility/access rules.
  • Dedup and exclusion handled on BE (FE only renders).
  • No archiving logic in this endpoint — the same-CID cascade is owned by the external worker.

Result (Implementation)

Implemented in PR #1875 (feat/1874-related-by-cid):

  • POST /v1/tours/related-by-cid — Controller → DTO → Action → Repository slice, mirroring PreCheckBatchArchiveController.
  • RelatedToursByCidDto — same filter payload as batch archive + limit (default 50, capped at 100).
  • GetRelatedToursByCidAction — target resolution mirrors batch-archive rules; CID display resolution (cid_rename > google_views_cid > 1_cid); empty result set returns related_tours: [] with HTTP 200 (fail-open), never an error.
  • TourRelatedByCidRepository — only DB access point: target CID rows, related rows (delete_space = 0, targets excluded, limit + order by business_name), single grouped panorama-count query.
  • Tests: tests/Actions/Tours/GetRelatedToursByCidActionTest.php — 10 tests; full tests/Actions/Tours suite 413 OK.

E2E verified (11 scenarios) against the testergothru@gmail.com account (user 31611, sample CID 12546236414864652428 with 8 non-archived tours): target exclusion, multi-select exclusion, unique-CID empty result, limit behavior, empty payload, invalid type_select (409), missing/invalid token (401), cross-user IDs (empty — no leak), all mode via query-param search, and exceptionIds semantics (excluded targets that share a CID are returned as related).
